why: This repository is PUBLIC. Every tracked path is published to every clone, forever, and `git rm` does not un-publish history. The rules below are the classes of path that reached `main` once and must not reach it again: per-PR review residue, a directory named for scratch work, build output, an embedded git worktree, dev-home or secret material, an absolute path into the maintainer's real machine, and a reference to a system that is not public. Each is cheap to add by accident (a `git add -A` is enough) and expensive to remove.
how_to_fix_a_red: Delete the path, or move it somewhere the repo already publishes deliberately. Do NOT add it to `allowed` to make CI green unless you can write a rationale a stranger reading the public repo would accept — `allowed` is for paths whose name matches a rule but whose CONTENT is deliberately published, and every entry is reviewed as policy, not as a build fix.

path_rules.name: residue-name
path_rules.rationale: A path segment that IS a residue word, or a residue word followed by a delimiter. This is the rule that `temp-screenshots/` (80 files, 20.8 MB of per-PR before/after evidence) and `scratch/` (38 files, two sibling repositories' content) both broke. Delimiter-anchored on purpose so ordinary names that merely START with a residue word stay green: `template.py` and `bakeoff.py` do not match, and `tests/test_residue_name_rule_does_not_fire_on_template_or_bakeoff` pins that.

path_rules.name: residue-suffix
path_rules.rationale: Editor backups and the conflict-resolution droppings of `git merge`/`patch`. None is ever content; each is produced by a tool the contributor did not mean to commit from.

path_rules.name: build-output-or-cache
path_rules.rationale: Regenerable output. Committing it makes every clone carry a frozen copy that silently shadows a fresh build — the exact failure mode `src/personalclaw/static/dist` exists as a SYMLINK to avoid (see AGENTS.md, mechanical gotchas). `.gitignore` covers these; this rule is what catches a `git add -f` or a new directory the ignore rules do not yet name.

path_rules.name: embedded-repo-or-editor-state
path_rules.rationale: `.worktrees/` is the worst of these: `git add -A` stages each linked worktree as a GITLINK pointing at a local absolute path that exists on no other machine, and git warns that clones 'will not contain the contents of the embedded repository and will not know how to obtain it'. The artefact is a broken clone for every user, produced by the most ordinary contributor reflex there is (#3413). The rest is per-user editor and tool state that is not repo content.

path_rules.name: dev-home-or-secret-material
path_rules.rationale: A dev home holds LIVE credential material — `.local_secret`, `session_key`, `sel_hmac.key` — so committing one publishes working secrets, not just clutter. `.gitignore` globs these; this rule is the second lock, because the cost of one miss is not recoverable by deleting forward.

path_rules.name: dotenv-with-real-values
path_rules.rationale: `.env` and `.env.local` are where real keys live. `.env.example` is deliberately tracked and deliberately NOT matched by this pattern: it is the documented template and carries only commented-out placeholders (`sk-ant-...`, `xoxb-...`). `tests/test_the_tracked_env_example_carries_no_real_value` re-checks that claim rather than trusting it.

path_rules.name: internal-planning-draft
path_rules.rationale: Launch planning drafts are internal by their own declaration — all four files removed in this change carried a literal `**State:** draft, internal, not published` header while being served from a PUBLIC repository, and none was linked from any published page. One of them (`prechannel-arrival-baseline.md:15`) additionally published the exact scope set of a live personal access token (`gist, read:org, repo, workflow`), which tells a reader precisely what a stolen token would grant. The token itself was never in the file. This rule is a path rule rather than a content rule because the directory is the unit of the decision: `docs/launch/` is where launch planning is drafted, and drafting is not publishing. If a launch document is genuinely meant for readers, it belongs on personalclaw.dev or in `docs/guides/`, not here.

binary_size_rule.name: oversized-binary
binary_size_rule.rationale: A tracked binary is permanent, unshrinkable weight in every clone (no Git LFS here). Measured ceiling after the publication-hygiene pass: the largest tracked binary is `docs/brand/social-preview.png` at 352 KB, and `docs/screenshots/` tops out at 328 KB. 512 KB is one step above that measured max — the same 'one step above measured, forbid growth' shape the structural ratchets use. It would have red `temp-screenshots/graph-cap/before-after-harness.png` (1.80 MB), the single largest file the repo ever tracked. TEXT files are exempt: CHANGELOG.md is 704 KB and grows legitimately.

real_home_path_rule.name: real-home-path
real_home_path_rule.rationale: An absolute path into a real developer's home publishes the author's username and machine layout. This is an ALLOWLIST of placeholder home names rather than a denylist of real ones, for two reasons: a denylist would have to write the maintainer's username INTO the public repo to keep it out (self-defeating), and an allowlist reds an unrecognised name the first time it appears instead of only the names someone already thought of. The listed names are the complete measured set across the tracked tree — every one a synthetic fixture (`/Users/x`, `/home/u`, `/Users/dev`) or a dev-home path fragment (`/home/config.json`). Adding a name here is a claim that it is a PLACEHOLDER, not a person. `linuxbrew` and `lb` are claimed as placeholders on the same measured basis: `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew` is Homebrew-on-Linux's canonical install prefix, byte-identical on every machine and named in Homebrew's own documentation, so it publishes nothing about this author; and `lb` is an unprivileged account that `scripts/fresh_install_validate.sh` CREATES inside a throwaway container (`chown -R lb:lb`, `su lb -c`) because Homebrew refuses to run as root — it is a fixture of the script, not a person's home.

internal_reference_rule.name: internal-reference
internal_reference_rule.rationale: This repository is public, and the name, host, identifier or document of a system that is NOT public says something about where the code was written that the code never needs to say. Measured before this rule: eight tree lines cited one non-public document by its content id and forty-two named the guidance system it came from, alongside that system's numbered control ids, the CLI of a non-public sign-in tool, a non-public desktop app's bundle id, and a non-public team and service used as test fixtures — across source comments, test docstrings, docs and the CHANGELOG. Every one carried a real reason, and every reason survives without the citation: 'never trust an upload's declared type; cap what it can make us decode' is the principle, and the title of the document that taught it adds nothing a reader can use. The denylist is salted SHA-256 digests of canonical candidates, because a plaintext list would publish the names it exists to keep out — the self-defeat the home-path rule avoids by being an allowlist. Six kinds: `word` (a whole letter-and-digit run, case-folded), `phrase` (two consecutive words, checked only behind a `phrase-head` digest of the first), `host` (every suffix of a dotted run, so a denied host denies its subdomains), `code` (letters, an optional hyphen and one to three digits, digits folded to 9), and `id` (a three-letter prefix and a 14-character mixed-case or 8-character lowercase tail, folded to prefix and shape). Each kind carries one CONTROL entry whose plaintext the suite assembles at runtime, so a green run proves every kind fires against this very file. Every tracked path and every text file is checked; binary content is not decoded, for the reason the home-path rule gives.
internal_reference_rule.how_to_fix: An internal-reference finding is fixed by rewriting the sentence to state the PRINCIPLE instead of naming its source — 'never trust an upload's declared type; cap decoded size and page count', not a document's title or id — and by renaming a fixture that borrows a non-public team, service or app name. There is no exemption for this rule: a match is always a defect. To deny a new name, run `python3 scripts/check_publication_hygiene.py --digest KIND TEXT` and add the printed digest(s) to `internal_reference_rule.denied`; never write the plaintext into the repository, a commit message, a PR or an issue. Before publishing text outside the tree (a PR body, a release note, an unpacked wheel), `--scan PATH` checks it the same way.

allowed.rationale: Matches `residue-name` on its `debug_` prefix, but the word is descriptive of what it does, not a mark of residue: it is a documented manual on-host sandbox check (listed in `tests/README.md`) that prints the detected backend and confirms `~/.aws/` is blocked. Present since the initial public commit and referenced from the tests README. Kept broad-rule-plus-exception rather than narrowing the pattern, so the NEXT `debug_*` file that appears reds and forces a deliberate decision.
